text.p: The lira closed steady at 104,160 against the dollar on Friday.
Bankers said it opened easier at 104,330, but firmed due to the dollar's fall against the mark on world markets.

The central bank set its dollar rate for banks' compulsory foreign currency transfers at 104,200 lira at the opening, after Thursday's 104,050 lira close, but decreased it gradually to 104,000 at the close as the dollar slipped abroad.

The money market opened with a 54.4 trillion lira surplus. Overnight money traded at between 57 and 77.50 percent in the day and the central bank drained 12.6 trillion lira at 57 percent overnight at close.
It had drained 3.7 trillion overnight at 57 percent on Thursday when the average money rate was 72.27.
The central bank lent banks 25.5 trillion lira via t/n value deals at 74 percent, down from the 32.1 trillion lira it injected on Thursday.
Yields on t-bills and bonds eased up to one point on continued liquidity.

The average yield on the most heavily traded June 4, 1997 paper eased to 112.70 from Thursday's 113.82 percent. The second most active September 3, 1997 paper yielded 113.62, down from Thursday's 113.70 percent average.
